text.text: Three masterplans, each told in the same nine steps.
Chapter 02 found the problems in one walkable area on each island. This chapter proposes a masterplan for each of those areas that answers them.
Each masterplan area is about 400 m across. Each plan decides what to rebuild, what to keep and what to repair, and treats the area as one place, not as separate projects.
The three plans follow the same steps in the same order. A reader can stop at any step and turn to the same step on another island.
THE RULES EVERY PLAN KEEPS TO
the largest footprint for one block
storeys, the most for any block
storeys on a student’s capstone plot
THE STEPS IN EACH PLAN
The colour pairs mark the six layers. Each layer keeps its colour on all three islands.
Divider
The plan’s name, and what it answers.
Vision
The one idea, its strategies, and the numbers before and after.
Parti
The idea as a diagram, in numbered steps.
Existing conditions
What stands on the site today: what stays and what goes.
Movement network
Who moves where, and what changes for a person on foot.
Public and green space
Where the shared space is, and how much there is per person.
Non-residential
What the area offers besides homes, and who it serves.
Residential
How many homes, of what kind, and for whom.
Masterplan
The layers put back together as one plan.
Policy and guidelines
The rules that make the plan hold.
